# dsh-model-retry-settings
A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin: a **max retries** control on the web GUI's **Settings → Model** pag

e, the one preference the shipped composition has no surface for.
**English** | 简体中文

**Request retries** — one card at the foot of **Settings → Model** that decides
how many times a fai

led model request is retried, for every provider in the
profile.
## What it does

dsh resolves a request-retry policy **per provider route**: an adapter's
`providerRetryPolicy()` is

captured when that route registers
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/retry-policy`), the agent loop carries the

resolved policy
into the `agent/request-error` waterfall on every failed attempt, and the
optional

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry` plugin executes it as durable `llm/retry`
events. Nothing in the shippe

d composition lets a person change that number
without hand-editing provider configuration.
This plugin owns the preference instead:

- it rides **its own Loader entry's `Config`** as its settings namespace — since
dsh 0.1.7 an entry'

s Config *is* its settings namespace, so both fields are
`.volatile()` and become writable through t

he ordinary settings transport;
- the browser half renders the control into the Models page's design

, `settings.models.footer`;
- the host half rewrites the policy the retry executor is about to read.
| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | While off, every provider's own retry policy applies untouched. |
|
`maxRetries` | integer 0–50 | `5` | Retries one failed model request may make. `0` disables retryin
xRetries` | integer 0–50 | `5` | Retries one failed model request may make. `0` disables retrying. |

`5` is dsh's own shipped default (`DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/retry-policy`), so

a fresh install behaves like a stock one
until you change the value.

## How the override lands

The host half registers one listener on the `agent/request-error` waterfall with
`{ prepend: true }`

. `ctx.waterfall` composes listeners **outermost-first**, so a
prepended listener runs before the re

try executor registered by `dsh-base` — and
the substituted policy is what that executor destructure

s out of the very same
payload object:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Everything mechanical stays with `dsh-llm-retry`: the durable retry counter and
its `sessionProjecti

ons` state, the backoff schedule, and the `llm/retry` /
`llm/retry-started` session events the traje

ctory renders. This plugin changes
only the number.
Consequences worth knowing:

- **Only `mode: 'normal'` policies carry a `maxRetries`.** An `always` policy is
left exactly as its

provider declared it, and so is an absent policy.
- **The value replaces, not caps.** Setting it ab

ove a provider's declared budget
raises it; the provider's `retryPolicyKey` changes with it, so the

durable retry
counter tracks the new policy cleanly.
- **Without `dsh-llm-retry` composed, the prefe

rence has no effect** — with no
executor, no request is retried at all. `dsh-llm-retry` is in `dsh-b

ase`, so
every shipped profile has it.
- Volatile values are updated **in place** on the running fib

er, so the listener
reads the current value on every failure: no subscription, no re-`apply()`, no
r
estart. The Settings page's own save is the only write.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Why |
| DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.2.3-0` | the range this plugin is built and verified against (0.

2.2-rc.1); the card needs the Models settings page's `settings.models.footer` seat |
| Node `>=24.9.

0` | the range declared in `package.json` (`engines`) |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry` composed | th

e retry executor itself; it ships inside `dsh-base`, so every stock profile has it |
| Google Chrome
, for `node tools/preview.mjs` only | the preview harness renders the card outside the GUI and scree

nshots it with headless Chrome; neither the plugin nor the suites need a browser |
| Node, for `sh s
cripts/verify.sh` | plus the DeepSeek Harness desktop app and network access on its first run, see b
/verify.sh` | plus the DeepSeek Harness desktop app and network access on its first run, see below |

`sh scripts/verify.sh` takes the real `@deepseek-ai/*` packages out of the
installed desktop app's `

app.asar`, so it needs that app present (set `DSH_ASAR`
for a non-default location) and network acce

ss on its first run. The client
packages the web shell inlines as platform seeds (`dsh-client-ui-pri

mitives`,
`dsh-client-ui-slots`, `dsh-client-store`) are no longer installed under the
app's `node_m

odules`, so the harness fetches those three from npm pinned to the
installation's own version. For t

hat reason the suites are not wired into hosted
CI: this repository ships no workflow, and `sh scrip

ts/verify.sh` is the gate you
run on a machine that has DeepSeek Harness installed.
## Install

This repository is a standalone plugin package: `lib/index.js` (host) and
`lib/client.js` (browser)
are committed in the forms dsh loads them in.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

For the **desktop** profile the app owns the profile, so `dsh plugin add` refuses
it: install the pa

cked tarball from **Settings → Plugins**, or hand
`dist/dsh-model-retry-settings-<version>.tgz` to t
he plugin-manager tool.
Two things are load-bearing:

- **Install the tarball, not the directory.** A `link:` dependency points outside
the profile's `nod

e_modules`, so the harness host can only reach it once it has
registered that path as a linked root

— which happens at boot. A packed tarball
installs as a real directory under `<profile>/node_modules

/`, the same shape a
registry plugin has, so the installation's module-interception layer resolves
i

ts `@deepseek-ai/*` peers the moment the profile loads it.
- **Restart the harness after adding it.*
